title: inflight-debugger-and-oncall-brief-compiler
author: Aisha Patel
description: Adds two complementary on-call utilities to incident-bot: an "inflight debugger" command that spins up a short-lived debug session (sandboxed, scoped credentials) tied to a specific alert context, and a compact 'oncall brief compiler' which generates a single-page incident brief by aggregating alert metadata, recent logs, top traces, and a tl;dr action checklist. Motivation: oncall pages often lose signal between alerts and a quick root-cause reproduction path; engineers spend time manual-ing together links and commands. This feature reduces time-to-first-action by providing curated, executable context and a safe ephemeral exec path for live debugging during escalations. Key user stories: - As an oncall, I want a one-line command that returns a short incident brief (summary, top suspects, suggested commands) so I can decide next steps quickly. - As an escalation lead, I want to spawn a temporary, audited debug session with read-only sampling tokens so I can run diagnostic queries without exposing long-lived credentials. Design choices and constraints: - Ephemeral sessions are implemented as temporary JWTs with 15-minute TTL, minted by the incident-bot service using existing KMS integrations. Tokens are recorded in the audit log and are scoped to allowed namespaces. - The brief compiler uses a prioritized fetch pipeline: alert metadata -> recent spans (100s) -> top error logs (N=20) -> KV cache of historical runbook hits -> generate a 6-line TL;DR and a 3-step suggested mitigation. - Output formats: plain text brief for terminal, and JSON --brief for integrations (pager, Slack). - Security: tokens are never printed in plain logs; the ephemeral-debugger performs an additional confirm step and requires two approvals if the target environment is production. - Telemetry: added metrics for brief generation latency, token issuance rate, and ephemeral session acceptance/denial counts. Backward compatibility: optional flags are used; default behavior is read-only and non-invasive. Checklist: - [x] Implement brief compiler pipeline and CLI flags - [x] Implement ephemeral token issuance and audit hooks - [x] Add unit and integration tests for token scoping and TTL - [x] Add e2e scenario in CI that simulates an oncall flow - [x] Add docs and a short quickstart snippet to incident-bot README Known limitations: - Brief compiler relies on the presence of indexed traces; for services without tracing the brief omits the top-trace section and falls back to recent logs. - Current session sandbox supports bash commands only; future work will add curated command sets and step replay. Related work: ENG-9813 (oncall briefing initiative), ENG-9881 (ephemeral auth patterns), SUP-4122 (customer request for safer debug sessions).

review_comments: Diego Morales: Can the brief include a cached 'previous action' field from the last 24h incidents? Might help reduce duplicated work.
Aisha Patel: Added a compact previous_actions section to the brief pipeline; falls back to empty if none found. Stored in brief_compiler KV cache with 24h TTL.
Rina Cho: Security question: what prevents a user from reusing an ephemeral token? Need to bind tokens to the request id and user-agent.
Aisha Patel: Tokens are now bound to request_id and user_id; middleware rejects tokens with mismatched binding. Added tests to validate binding enforcement.
Samir Kapoor: Integration tests flaky on CI when traces are unavailable; suggest mocking trace backend for deterministic result.
Aisha Patel: CI change added a 'trace-fixture' stub for e2e; job will skip trace assertions if the fixture reports not-available (counts as covered).
merge_summary: Squash-merged after approval from reviewers and a successful CI run. Rollout gated behind feature flag `brief_compiler.enabled` and `ephemeral_debug.enabled`. Feature flags default to off in production; ramping plan created in ENG-9813.
release_notes: Added 'incident-bot brief' to produce concise incident briefs and 'incident-bot infight-debug' to create short-lived, audited debug sessions. These are behind feature flags and require RBAC for production usage.
